newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq sees oil shipped to world markets next week.
newsitem.headline: Iraq sees oil shipped to world markets next week.

text.p: The first Iraqi oil since the Gulf War could be shipped to world markets next week now that Baghdad had signed deals with 50 companies to sell its crude under a U.N. oil-for-food deal, an oil official said on Tuesday.
"No problem remains...The story is over...loading is supposed to start next week," Taha Hmud Mosa, senior under-secretary at Iraq's oil ministry, told Reuters.

Mosa said Iraq had signed "initial contracts" with 50 international firms for the oil sales, putting Iraqi oil onto world markets for the first time since sanctions were imposed for invading Kuwait in 1990.

"We have deals with 50 firms from Europe, South East Asia and South America...These are initial but binding international contracts. They do not include prices as prices have to be determined at the time of shipping," he said.
Mosa said the deals could be completed "in several days as the companies are ready waiting for the signal to start loading."

He said experts from a Dutch firm were due in Baghdad on Tuesday. Their experts would inspect Iraq's twin pipeline via Turkey to ensure previously faulty equipment at Iraq's Zakho station near the Turkish border was now operational.

A team from Lloyd's Shipping Intelligence left Baghdad on Tuesday following an inspection tour of Iraq's trade outlets. They had paved the way for U.N. inspections of humanitarian supplies reaching Iraq under the oil deal.

Mosa said Iraq's export outlets were capable of handling 2.4 million barrels of oil per day (bpd), almost three times the amount Baghdad would be allowed to export under its food-for-oil deal with the U.N..
"Mina al-Bakr is ready one hundred percent. Through it we can export 1.2 million bpd. Through the second outlet via Ceyhan in Turkey, we can export also about 1.2 million bpd," he said.

He said Iraq intended to use both outlets simultaneously once the United Nations gives it the go-ahead to start the exports under the partial export deal whose conditions Baghdad accepted on November 25.
Iraq, he said, had the ability to produce 2.5 million barrels of oil per day (bpd) and could boost the figure to three million in three months.
The limited oil sales, designed to ease the suffering of the Iraqi people under U.N. trade sanctions, allow Baghdad $2 billion of exports in six months.
Mosa said Iraq intended to ship about 350,000 bpd via Mina al-Bakr on the Gulf and an estimated 450,000 bpd through Turkey depending on world oil prices.
He said the export capacity of Gulf terminals could be raised to 1.6 million bpd "in the near future after the completion of certain requirements."
Mosa said Iraq was also planning to regain the original capacity of its twin pipeline via Turkey of 1.6 million bpd.
"One of the main (pumping) stations was bombed. This station can be restored in a few months and the capacity boosted to 1.6 million," he said.
